question_text: State and prove the principle of conservation of angular momentum. Explain the principle with examples.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The statement
lines: If no external torque acts on a system,

steps.margin_note: The condition "no external torque" is half the statement — the law is false without it.
steps.why: This is the rotational twin of conservation of linear momentum, with torque playing the role force played there.
common_mistakes: Stating it without the no-external-torque condition.

recall.must_convey: That with no external torque, the total angular momentum stays constant.
accept: no external torque so L is constant
reject: torque is d L by d t

steps.memory_tip: The rotational twin of momentum conservation: no external TORQUE → L is constant.

lines: Torque is the rate of change of angular
If the external torque is zero,
steps.margin_note: Three lines: the definition of torque, set it to zero, read off the constancy. Finish with I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂ — the form the examples use.
steps.why: The proof is one definition plus one substitution — but the final form Iω = constant is what does all the explaining: shrink I and ω must grow.
common_mistakes: Proving it for constant I only. The law holds even while I changes — that is its whole point.

recall.must_convey: That τ = dL/dt, zero torque makes L constant, so I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂.
accept: torque is d L by d t

steps.memory_tip: τ = dL/dt; put τ = 0 and Iω = constant follows.

steps.margin_note: Each example must SAY which quantity changed and which way — "I down, ω up" — not just name the dancer.
steps.why: The dancer is conservation with I changing; the helicopter is conservation with L exchanged between parts. Two different faces of the same law.
common_mistakes: Naming the examples without the I-and-ω reasoning, which earns nothing.

recall.must_convey: That the folding dancer (I down, ω up) and the helicopter tail rotor are the examples.

steps.memory_tip: Two examples, two mechanisms: the dancer changes I (arms in → spins faster); the helicopter needs a tail rotor because L is exchanged between its parts.
